content_voiceover: This forest plot is a meta-analysis pooling four randomized trials of DOACs against low molecular weight heparin in cancer associated thrombosis, including edoxaban, rivaroxaban, and two apixaban trials, Raskob, Young, McBane, and Agnelli. For recurrent VTE on top, the pooled risk ratio is zero point six two with a confidence interval of zero point four three to zero point nine one, favoring DOACs, and the diamond sits clearly to the left of one with a significant p value of zero point zero one. For major bleeding on the bottom, the pooled risk ratio is one point three one with a confidence interval of zero point eight three to two point zero eight, so the diamond straddles one and this difference is not statistically significant, p equals zero point two five. Putting this together with the individual trials you just saw, the consistent message across the literature is that DOACs reduce recurrent thrombosis in cancer patients compared to LMWH, and while there is a trend toward more bleeding, that trend does not reach significance when trials are pooled, which is why current guidelines now endorse DOACs as an appropriate option for many cancer associated thrombosis patients, with caution still warranted in GI and genitourinary malignancies.
keypoints: Meta-analysis of four DOAC vs LMWH trials in cancer associated thrombosis
Pooled recurrent VTE risk ratio 0.62, significantly favors DOACs (p=0.01)
Pooled major bleeding risk ratio 1.31, not statistically significant (p=0.25)
Pooled data support DOACs as an appropriate CAT treatment option
Caution still warranted in GI and genitourinary cancers
keypoint_voiceover: This meta-analysis of four trials found DOACs significantly reduce recurrent VTE, risk ratio zero point six two, with a nonsignificant trend toward more major bleeding, risk ratio one point three one, supporting current guidance to use DOACs in cancer associated thrombosis with caution in GI and GU malignancies.
